author: Lydia Kulbida
title: Round Up at the Register campaign kicks off at Market 32, Price Chopper - NewsBreak
text:
By Lydia Kulbida Natalie St. Denis ,
1 hours ago
ALBANY, N.Y. ( NEWS10 ) -- Every year during hurricane season, Market 32 and Price Chopper asks customers to Round Up at the Register to support the work of the American Red Cross Disaster Relief Fund. But even if hurricanes don't reach the Capital Region, the Red Cross remains active here after recent historic flooding, home fires, as well as by making sure blood is available for anyone who needs it.
Download our WTEN+ streaming app on Roku, Fire TV and Apple TV! A simple reminder is posted at registers throughout Market 32 and Price Chopper stores, encouraging customers to round up their bill, with the extra change going directly to the Red Cross. Market 32 Price Chopper is matching the first $10,000 and customers' donations can add to the total now through September 30. Last year's campaign raised nearly $88,000 and the goal this year is $100,000.
"We at Market 32 Price Chopper are part of this community, and we've seen the stories on NEWS10 about flooding right here in this region," said Market 32 and Price Chopper Vice President of Communications and Public Affairs Mona Golub. "So we know it's not just about neighbors across the country, it's about our neighbors and friends right here at home and we have this opportunity to help them. And our generous customers are ready to help too."
The local chapter of the Red Cross Eastern New York Region opened four emergency shelters during this summer's flooding in the Capital Region. This provided immediate assistance, as well as multi-resource centers to connect people with more help on the road to recovery.
Get the latest news, weather, sports and entertainment delivered right to your inbox! Red Cross Board Member Chris Greagun pointed out that all of the shelters are staffed by volunteers.
"Neighbors helping neighbors, providing shelter, providing food, helping when people are at their worst, the Red Cross is there," Greagun said.
This summer, the Red Cross declared its second ever national blood supply crisis . As a result, more people are rolling up their sleeves and Red Cross Regional Chief Executive Officer Kevin Coffey said you never know who you might help by doing so.
"When a new mother is in a hospital giving birth, she should have blood products available if she needs it, or if there's a car accident, that family member should not have to wait for blood products to be available. We never want to be in a shortage situation, the best is to regularly schedule your blood donations," Coffey said.
